assessments.zone: Rural villages of Mosango secteur (Mosango and Yasa Bonga health zones) in northern part of the unit: Kambu/Muluma, Tumikia Mission, Koshi Muluwa, Kimputu, Kimolo, Kumbi, Mikwati, Kipasi, etc.
assessments.evidence: Mosango secteur, between Masi-Manimba centre and the Bulungu/Bagata borders, has no reported armed-group control; occasional Mobondo-related alarms in Kwilu concern western Bagata rather than Mosango. Ordinary state authority with PNC as main force is assumed. Web research was unavailable for this run (web search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the proxy), so this rests on prior knowledge and regional reports cited by neighbouring assessments.

assessments.zone: Main centres of the unit: Pay (Pay Kongila HZ, Moanza secteur), Leta (Kingungi HA) and Basuku/Mosango (Mosango secteur and health-zone seat), each above ~10,000 inhabitants
assessments.evidence: No armed group is known to hold territory in the Moanza or Mosango secteurs of Masi-Manimba; the Mobondo militia active since 2022 operates further west (Kwamouth, western Bagata, Kwango river) and has not been reported ruling localities here. Pay (Pay Kongila health-zone seat) and Basuku (Mosango secteur/health-zone seat) are administrative centres with PNC posts; Leta is a large village in Moanza health zone where a PNC post is assumed rather than documented and territorial administration, so the PNC is the main permanent force. Web research was unavailable for this run (web search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the proxy), so this rests on prior knowledge and regional reports cited by neighbouring assessments. Review 2026-10-01: not independently verified.

assessments.zone: Rural villages of Moanza secteur (Moanza, Pay Kongila, Mosango and Kingandu health zones) south of the Kwilu/Kwenge rivers: Kisumbu, Kingola, Lundu, Mbenga, Tsaku Meya, Mosambo, Kinzenzengo, Kulungu, Moanza village, etc.
assessments.evidence: Remote rural area of southern Masi-Manimba with no reported armed-group control; order rests on customary chiefs and PNC/ANR posts at secteur and groupement level. The Mobondo theatre lies well to the west and north-west and no Mobondo incursion here is known as of the reference date. Web research was unavailable for this run (web search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the proxy), so this rests on prior knowledge and regional reports cited by neighbouring assessments.

assessments.zone: Yasa-Bonga secteur (northern Masi-Manimba territory: Mafwa, Pupu, Mungoto, Yelenge, Dunda Bac, Saka Centre, Kwaya Centre etc., Yasa Bonga and Vanga health zones)
assessments.evidence: No armed-group activity is reported in the Yasa-Bonga secteur, which lies between Bagata (Mobondo-affected only in its far western fringe) and Bulungu/Vanga; ordinary state authority with PNC posts and customary chiefs is assumed. Live web research was unavailable for this run (web search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the proxy), so this rests on prior knowledge and regional reports cited by neighbouring assessments.

assessments.zone: Central, eastern and southern Masi-Manimba secteur villages along the RN1 and toward Mosango/Moanza (Kitsamanga, Kiko, Lumbi Daniel, Mosenge, Kimbiki etc.)
assessments.evidence: No reports of armed-group control located for these villages; state authority via PNC posts, territorial administration and customary chiefs is assumed. Neighbouring Bulungu territory to the east is likewise assessed as calm. Live web research was unavailable for this run (web search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the proxy), so this rests on prior knowledge and regional reports cited by neighbouring assessments.

assessments.zone: Western Masi-Manimba secteur toward the Kwango/Kenge and Bagata borders (Kimbinga, Kiwawa Pont, Kiwawa Kapadi, Munzabala, Kifunga Centre and Moanza health zone villages, lon < 17.8)
assessments.evidence: The Mobondo militia spread from Kwamouth into Bagata, Kenge and other areas along the Kwango in 2023-2025 and holdouts were still raiding in mid-2026 despite an August 2026 peace process; this western fringe is the part of the unit nearest that theatre, so occasional incursions cannot be excluded. No locality here is known to be under lasting Mobondo rule, so ordinary state authority (PNC posts, customary chiefs) is assumed. Live web research was unavailable for this run (web search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the proxy), so this rests on prior knowledge and regional reports cited by neighbouring assessments. No source located specifically documents Mobondo raids inside Masi-Manimba territory; the raiding flag reflects proximity to the Kenge/Bagata theatre only.

assessments.zone: Masi-Manimba town, territorial seat on the RN1 (Masi Manimba health zone)
assessments.evidence: Territorial seat with territorial administration, PNC commissariat and courts on the Kinshasa-Kikwit RN1; no armed group is reported to hold the town. The December 2023 elections here were annulled over fraud and violence, but that unrest did not displace state authority. The Mobondo militia theatre (Kwamouth, western Bagata, Kenge) lies to the west. Live web research was unavailable for this run (web search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the proxy), so this rests on prior knowledge and regional reports cited by neighbouring assessments.

units.CD3212-masi-manimba-2: This unit covers the Moanza and Mosango secteurs of Masi-Manimba territory (Kwilu), a rural area including the Moanza, Pay Kongila, Mosango and parts of the Kingandu and Yasa Bonga health zones, with Pay, Leta and Basuku (Mosango) as main centres. No armed group is known to exercise territorial control here; the Mobondo militia that spread from Kwamouth since 2022 affects mainly western Bagata, Kwamouth and the Kwango river area, and its holdouts were still raiding there in mid-2026. All localities are assessed as under ordinary state authority with the PNC as main permanent force. Web research was unavailable for this run, so confidence is low for rural villages. A skeptical review (2026-10-01) could not run independent web searches (search budget exhausted, news and search sites blocked by the proxy); zone assignments were checked against adm3/health-zone data and coordinates (western Moanza villages at ~17.5E lie east of the Kwango river, away from the Mobondo theatre) and the default-state-presence assessment is retained unverified, consistent with neighbouring Masi-Manimba-1, Bulungu, Gungu and Kenge units.
units.CD3212-masi-manimba-1: Masi-Manimba territory part 1 (Kwilu) covers the Masi-Manimba and Yasa-Bonga secteurs, including Masi-Manimba town on the RN1 and the large settlement of Kimbinga. No armed group is reported to control any locality; the Mobondo militia theatre (Kwamouth, western Bagata, Kenge) lies to the west and holdouts were still raiding parts of the region in 2026, so the western fringe is flagged as exposed to raids. All locations are assessed as under ordinary state authority with the PNC as main permanent force. Live web research was unavailable for this run, so confidence is medium for the territorial seat and low elsewhere. Review (2026-10-01) could not re-verify with web research (search budget exhausted, AllAfrica/news sites blocked); zones kept, and the Mobondo 'raiding' flag on the western fringe is a proximity-based precaution rather than a documented incursion into this unit.
